standard_prerequisites.name: The Tutte-Berge formula for the number of unmatched vertices in a maximum matching
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used in the last line of the counted proof (source line 365, referring to the author's displayed formula eq:Tutte-Berge at source lines 240-241, itself attributed by the author to Bollobas at line 238)
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the bound q <= |U| on the number of odd components of the graph minus U into the existence of a matching covering all vertices when the order is even and all but at most one vertex when the order is odd.

core_obligations: Let the odd components of Gamma - U be Q_1, ..., Q_q with q = odd(Gamma - U) and treat U empty separately: then q = 0 for even vertex count and q = 1 for odd vertex count, which already gives the two required coverings (proof lines 346-348).
For non-empty U every Q_i is proper and non-empty, so the spectral hypothesis lambda(Gamma) >= d-1 gives e_Gamma(Q_i, Q_i^c) >= d-1 (proof lines 349-352).

Parity upgrade: d-regularity gives d|Q_i| = 2 e_Gamma(Q_i) + e_Gamma(Q_i, Q_i^c), so the cut size is congruent to d modulo 2, and since d-1 has the opposite parity it must be at least d (proof lines 353-359).

Double counting: each of the q odd components sends its at least d edges into U, and all these edges lie in the d|U| edges incident with U, so qd <= sum_i e_Gamma(Q_i,U) <= d|U| and hence q <= |U| (proof lines 360-363).
Apply the Tutte-Berge formula to the bound q <= |U| to conclude a perfect matching for even order and a nearly-perfect matching for odd order (proof lines 364-365).
proof_roadmap: 用谱条件把每个奇分量与补集的割至少压到 d-1，再用 d-正则性做奇偶提升到 d。
把 q 个奇分量发往 U 的边双重计数，得到 q <= |U|；最后套用 Tutte–Berge 公式得到偶阶完美匹配、奇阶近完美匹配。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the spectral matching lemma of the paper (author Lemma at source lines 339-342, label lem:regular-matching): a connected d-regular graph with lambda(Gamma) >= d-1 has a perfect matching when the order is even and a nearly-perfect matching when it is odd. Its proof (source lines 344-366) cannot be done by the routine textbook argument that would apply when no spectral hypothesis is present: the parity upgrade from the expansion estimate e_Gamma(Q_i, Q_i^c) >= d-1 to e_Gamma(Q_i, Q_i^c) >= d is the step that makes the double counting work, and it uses d-regularity in the form d|Q_i| = 2 e_Gamma(Q_i) + e_Gamma(Q_i, Q_i^c) together with the oddness of |Q_i| (proof lines 353-359). The closing step appeals to the Tutte-Berge formula for maximum matchings rather than to Hall's condition in the bipartite form. H2.
